To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exposure to multi-walled carbon nano tubes (MWCNT) via inhalation exacerbates myocardial infarct size after a subsequent myocardial infarctions.
oropharynx aspiration of three forms of MWTs exacerbate myocardial ischemic/reperfussion injury.
exposure to MWCNT exacerbates I/R injury without a significant lung inflammatory response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of MWCNT exposure on cardiac I/R injury.
the adverse health risks of exposure to carbon nanotubes.
the effects of exposure to MWCNTs on cardiac tissue and may have significant clinical implications for the use of MWCNT in biomedical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MWCNTs, in this particular model system, are not inert and may be harmful to the heart.
the MWCNTs, in particular the N-doped and COOH forms, have the potential to cause cardiac injury and should be further investigated.
exposure to MWCNTs by the oropharyngea route may increase the susceptibility of the cardiovascular system to ischemia/reperfuson injury and that this effect is dependent on the type of MWCNT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-doped MWNCTs are more potent than other forms of MWNCTs in promoting the cardiac I/R injury.
the pulmonary exposure to MWCNTs can exacerbate myocardial ischemia/reperfuion injury.
oropharygeal aspiration of MWNCTs may pose a risk to cardiovascular health and may have long lasting effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the form of MWNCTs used in this study, especially the N-doped form, has a significant impact on the severity of the cardiac I/R injury.
the form of MWNCT is an important determinant of the pulmonary and cardiac response to MWCN exposure.
exposure to MWCNTs can exacerbate I/R injury in a time-dependent manner and this is independent of the inflammatory response.
